title: Mold Remediation Billing Error, Duplicate Line and Goodwill Credits
content:
The job must be in cleared or invoiced status when an adjustment credit is posted on a Mold Remediation job. A billing error credit equals the amount charged on the line less the amount the tier's rate and the recorded quantity produce; a duplicate line credit equals the full amount of a line repeating another of the same code, date and quantity. A re-cleaning line billed after a failed clearance is credited in full as a billing error.

A billing error or duplicate line credit may be posted only when the customer raises the dispute no later than the dispute window after the final invoice was issued on this job. The dispute window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the job's invoice date, and a dispute raised on the last day of the window is in time; on a job not yet invoiced the window has not started and the dispute is always in time.

Goodwill credits on one job may not exceed the tier's goodwill credit cap in total. A goodwill request above the remaining cap is handed to a human representative as not covered by policy. Each charge line takes at most one adjustment credit.

## Questions the desk answers from this rule

**What does a billing error credit come to?** The amount charged on the line less the amount the tier's rate multiplied by the recorded quantity produces. Hypothetical: a line charged at 3.10 per square foot for 52 square feet (161.20) where the tier's rate is 2.35 produces 122.20, so the credit is 39.00.

**What does a duplicate line credit come to?** The full amount of the line that repeats another line of the same code, date and quantity.

**How is a re-cleaning line billed after a failed clearance treated?** It is credited in full as a billing error.

**When is the dispute in time?** Day 1 of the window is the day after the job's invoice date. With a 60-day window and an invoice dated 1 April, day 60 is 31 May: a dispute raised on 31 May is in time, one raised on 1 June is not. A dispute on a job not yet invoiced is always in time.

**How much goodwill may be posted?** In total on one job, no more than the tier's goodwill credit cap. Hypothetical: with a cap of 150.00 and 90.00 already posted as goodwill, the remaining cap is 60.00; a request for 60.00 may be posted, while a request for 75.00 is handed to a human representative as not covered by policy.

**Can one line take two credits?** No. Each charge line takes at most one adjustment credit.

**What records decide it?** The job's status and invoice date, the charge line being credited, and the goodwill credits already posted on the job, all as the company's records show them before the credit is posted.
